findings.title: Protective closure becomes blocking insulation
findings.claim: The focus makes the same boundary do opposite work in two supplied scenes: the cave's temporary closure protects the sleepers, while the coverings placed after refusal here block the route from reminder to comprehension.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries a reminder, turning away, and forgetting before جَعَلَ assigns covers and ear-weight; the exact 18:11 connection supplies the contrasting protective closure, so the causal history changes what the boundary does without removing the primary reading.
findings.reader_payoff: A covering is perceived as a functional boundary rather than a neutral image: it can preserve reception in one scene and insulate against reception in another.
findings.containment: The contrast is limited to the supplied 18:11 and 18:57 relation. It does not claim that the two closures have identical causes or that every covering is punitive.

epistemic.reason: The citable trusted finding supplies the four anchors, and the branch registry plus the exact 18:11 connection supply the focus carriers and wider trigger.

findings.containment: The feedback arrow is a qualified contextual reading from the legacy walk and the supplied relation. It does not settle whether the state is habit, consequence, or both.

findings.title: What is forgotten remains assigned to the hands
findings.claim: The forgotten thing is still the person's own prior act: the hand-expression binds what was sent ahead to its doer, while 78:40 turns the same relation into seeing it later. Forgetting therefore removes the deed from present recollection without removing its attribution.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins نَسِيَ to ما قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ; the exact 78:40 target repeats the hand-and-prior-deed relation with later seeing, activating the forgetting, prior-effect, and responsibility branches through the same expression.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgetting becomes a failure of present access to one's own record, not the deletion of what the hands have made.
findings.containment: The relation establishes retained attribution and later visibility, but does not specify a complete doctrine of record, judgment, or timing beyond the supplied parallel.

epistemic.reason: The focus word occurrences and branch records are exact, and conn_5efc00d03953032ba295 supplies exact Arabic for the wider hand-deed return; no unanchored reader summary is required.

findings.title: Guidance is offered before it is taken
findings.claim: The final clause separates being called toward guidance from attaining it: the goal is named and offered, while يَهْتَدُوا describes the recipients' own arrival; 27:81 supplies a wider parallel in which a call does not guide the blind.
findings.mechanism: The focus places الْهُدَىٰ after the directional call and then uses the Form VIII guidance verb under emphatic negation; the exact 27:81 connection returns through the same guidance field and distinguishes a call from the recipient's taking of its path.
findings.reader_payoff: The final negation is heard as a failed response to an available direction, not as proof that no guidance was presented.
findings.containment: This finding distinguishes offered direction and uptake within the supplied relation; it does not rank the two guidance words or settle a universal theory of guidance.

epistemic.reason: Both focus guidance occurrences and both core/extension facets are supplied, and conn_c866a4d70f50a9d1ebba provides exact Arabic for the wider call-versus-guidance relation.
